renderSubtitles.text:
Launch a ball at an angle,
and it flies in a curve.

That one curve is really two simple
motions, happening at once.

Across the ground, nothing pushes the ball sideways, so its
horizontal speed never changes. Equal steps, in equal times.

Up and down, gravity pulls on the ball, so its vertical
speed changes by the same amount every second.

It slows on the way up, stops for an instant at
the top, then speeds up on the way down.

Now orbit the path. The ground sees only the sideways
motion, and the pole sees only the up and down.

Put the two back together: at every moment, a sideways step
plus an up and down step makes one step along the curve.

Change the angle, and the same two
motions make a different curve.

Thirty and sixty degrees land in the same
place. Forty-five degrees goes farthest.

Change the speed, and the whole curve
scales: faster means higher and farther.

Independent components combine into
one path. That is the whole idea.
